prerequisites: It is recommended to have completed the core subjects of Industrial Drawing, Automatic Systems, Manufacturing Technologies, and Manufacturing Engineering (Manufacturing Technologies II and I of plan 434).

learning_outcomes.text: Basic knowledge of production and manufacturing systems.
Assimilates scientific, technological, and economic criteria for developing manufacturing systems and tooling.
Knows different types of production processes and can select the production process according to different parameters.
Applied knowledge of manufacturing systems and processes, metrology, and quality control.

Configures different types of manufacturing systems (flexible, dedicated) for various types of forming and measurement processes, highlighting the importance of inter- and intra-cell material handling.

Defines specifications, designs, and calculates the components that integrate forming and measurement workstations: structural, kinematic elements, actuators, monitoring-control; delving especially into the design of tooling in assembly processes (welding and mechanical joining).
Acquires practical skills in the design and calculation of components and tooling through the use of software applications characteristic of mechanical manufacturing engineering.
Acquires practical skills to program and control mechanical manufacturing systems through flexible automation.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, which enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills, and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans, and other similar tasks.
Ability to manage specifications, regulations, and mandatory standards.
Ability to apply quality principles and methods.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge, understanding, and ability to apply the necessary legislation in the exercise of the profession of Industrial Technical Engineer.

syllabus_topics: Workstations and cells for assembly processes
Industrial robots: selection, control, and programming
Mechanical design of manufacturing systems: mechanical assemblies, tooling, structures, piping, wiring
Programming and control using PLC/PC of automatisms based on electro-pneumatic circuits
teaching_methods: Technical case studies and problem solving

assessment_methods.method: Evaluation of skills related to practical sessions (direct observation and reports)
Evaluation of theoretical-practical knowledge related to the course content and technical cases (continuous controls)
Evaluation of the practical application of knowledge through a preliminary design project for a mechanical component assembly cell or through the analysis and improvement of a manufacturing system

assessment_rules: The student must be able to demonstrate authorship of the work/practical assignments in an oral interview; otherwise, the grade for these assignments will be 0. In case of not passing any of the gradual evaluation activities (a minimum grade of 4.0 is required in each), the global evaluation tests must be taken, which will be carried out during the period set by the center.
